I couldn't confirm the exact Node.js requirement for the latest Vitest release. The sources I found don't state it.

**Latest version:** The most recent stable release I found is v4.1.10. v4.1.10 | Stable appears in one release listing, but that listing doesn't give a date. A separate tracker shows v4.1.9 as the latest as of June 2026, so v4.1.10 may be newer. Check the GitHub releases page or npm for the current version.

**Node.js requirement:** The only explicit figure I found is an older one. Two pages list Vite >=v6.0.0, Node >=v20.0.0. These pages may predate Vitest 4, so they may not reflect the current requirement.

I did find that it supports Vite 8 from the start for Vitest 4.1. Vite 8 may carry its own Node.js requirement, which could be stricter than Vitest's, but I didn't find that information.

**To get a reliable answer:**
- Check the `engines` field in the `package.json` of the `vitest` package on npm.
- Check the official Vitest getting-started docs.
- Run `npm view vitest version` and `npm view vitest engines` to get the current values directly.

content.text:
According to the npm registry, the latest Vitest is **5.0.3**, and it requires Node.js **`^22.12.0 || ^24.0.0 || >=26.0.0`**. That means Node 22.12 or newer within the 22 line, any Node 24 release, or Node 26 and above. Node 20 and Node 23 are not supported, and neither is Node 25.

I took this from the `engines.node` field of the package's [npm registry entry](https://registry.npmjs.org/vitest/latest). The web search results only went up to Vitest 4.1.x and listed an older `Node >=v20.0.0` requirement, so they're out of date. The Ludion lesson base had nothing on this.

To check it yourself: `npm view vitest version engines`

Sources:
- [npm registry: vitest/latest](https://registry.npmjs.org/vitest/latest)
- [releases.sh – Vitest](https://releases.sh/vitest/vitest.md)
- [releasealert.dev – vitest-dev/vitest](https://releasealert.dev/github/vitest-dev/vitest)
- [Vitest 4.1 article](https://emeditor.it.com/a/7699.html)
